title: Beyond Predictable Paths: Redefining AI Security Incident Reporting for Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.24515v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI agents are being deployed rapidly, accompanied by a growing number of AI-specific attacks and corresponding incidents. As incident reporting becomes increasingly important for legal compliance, governance, accountability, and security; current frameworks must be adapted to the unique characteristics of AI agents. In this paper, two editorial authors compare AI systems and AI agents and, drawing on input from 23 experts in academia and industry, identify the information required for reporting incidents where the security of AI agents is harmed. %involving AI agents. Potential reporting elements include, for example, agent memory and memory accesses, actual and potential levels of autonomy, and tool usage. Based on these findings, we identify several open research questions, including how to efficiently record incidents and how to determine whether vulnerabilities and incidents generalize. translated_title: 超越可预测路径：重新定义面向智能体的AI安全事件报告
translated_abstract: AI智能体正在被快速部署，与此同时，针对AI的特定攻击和相关安全事件数量也在不断增长。随着事件报告在法律合规、治理、问责和安全方面的重要性日益提升，现有框架必须加以调整，以适应AI智能体的独特特征。在本文中，两位编辑作者对AI系统与AI智能体进行了比较，并借鉴来自学术界和产业界的23位专家的意见，识别出在AI智能体安全受到损害的事件报告中所需的信息。潜在的报告要素包括：智能体的记忆及记忆访问情况、实际与潜在的自主性水平，以及工具使用情况等。基于这些发现，作者提出了若干开放性研究问题，包括如何高效地记录事件，以及如何判断漏洞和事件是否具有普遍适用性。专家反馈还强调了潜在的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过对比AI系统与AI智能体并综合23位学术界和产业界专家的意见，重新定义了AI智能体安全事件报告框架，提出将智能体记忆及访问、自主性水平和工具使用等纳入报告要素，并指出高效记录事件与判断漏洞普遍性等开放研究问题。
en_tdlr: This paper redefines AI security incident reporting for AI agents by drawing on a comparison between AI systems and agents and input from 23 experts, proposing new reporting elements such as agent memory and access, autonomy levels, and tool usage, while identifying open research questions on efficient incident recording and vulnerability generalization.
